perspective:
Maria Ortega’s available information:

- She is a teacher at the community center and has a master’s degree.
- She and Cheryl Benallie are colleagues at the community center; they have worked together before and have been building a personal friendship.
- Maria noticed Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed with stacks of paperwork and planning for a new community outreach project.
- Maria offered to help Cheryl with the project, and Cheryl accepted.
- After helping, Maria observed that Cheryl handled her responsibilities better and seemed more confident.
- At a staff meeting, Maria suggested Cheryl for a leadership role on the next phase of the project, citing Cheryl’s aptitude and commitment.
- The team leader responded positively and asked Cheryl whether she wanted the role.
- Cheryl thanked Maria and said she was ready to take on the challenge.
- Maria worried that Cheryl might see the suggestion as overstepping, so she spoke to Cheryl privately.
- Maria told Cheryl she wanted her to feel supported, not pressured.
- Cheryl said she had been surprised but appreciated Maria’s support and felt it meant a lot that Maria believed in her.
- Maria felt relieved that Cheryl valued her honesty and support.
- Maria proposed that the two of them co-lead the project together.
- Cheryl agreed, saying Maria’s guidance had been invaluable and that they made a great team.
- They collaborated successfully on several projects, and Maria felt their partnership had strengthened.
- Maria was joyful about their synergy and suggested teaming up for more future projects.
- Cheryl said she would love that, called working with Maria a wonderful experience, and said she was excited about what they could achieve together.
